subject: Post-demo: workload breakdown & capacity follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@parcelco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T17:10:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: workload breakdown & capacity follow-up

Hi Samir / Katie —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end and a couple of asks so we can size a realistic PoC and recommend a deployment profile that meets your latency SLOs. Notes below are focused on capacity/throughput details we didn't fully lock during the demo.

High-level from call:
- Feature: user-facing streaming chat (web + mobile) for parcel tracking + follow-up Qs.
- Target latency: P95 <= 500ms for initial response chunk (streaming enabled).
- Observed UX: typical generated content ~200 tokens; some sessions include recent context (1–3 prior turns, ~600 tokens total).
- Expected steady usage: ~60 QPS (mostly web).
- Burst profile: short spikes up to ~600 QPS during peak usage events (30–90s), plus occasional 1–2 minute surges.
- Concurrency: rough estimate 700–900 concurrent streaming connections during peaks.

What we need from you to finalize sizing and PoC plan:
1) If possible, upload a 24–72h sampled trace (CSV or gz) showing timestamped requests, tokens_in, tokens_out, and response latencies. I attached a small template (workload-sample-template.csv) that matches the columns that help us compute tokens/sec and QPS buckets.
2) Confirm average prompt tokens vs full context tokens (you mentioned average generation ~200 tokens but some sessions go longer). If >300 tokens often, call it out.
3) Clarify streaming requirements: do you need partial token streaming as they are generated, or can we batch into 50–100 token chunks?

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus will draft a PoC capacity plan based on the trace you provide (expected deliverable: model recommendation + GPU counts, warm-pool sizing, and autoscale trigger thresholds).
- Schedule a 30–45 minute kickoff next week to agree on trace handoff and PoC timeline.

Attachments: workload-sample-template.csv (attached)

If you can drop the trace into the Drive link below (or send directly to me), Marcus and I will run an initial sketch and follow up with concrete numbers by EOD tomorrow after we receive the trace.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_sample-traces
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/2391

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Date: 2026-08-29T20:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: workload breakdown & capacity follow-up

Vanessa / Marcus —

Thanks for the clear recap. I uploaded a small sanitized sample trace (prod_trace_aug_sanitized.csv) — it's ~2 hours of traffic but representative of the last week's pattern. To confirm and add a few clarifications:

- Average generation tokens: ~200 tokens (median ~150), but 5–7% of requests have long answers (500+ tokens) during incident-handling flows.
- Context length: average context included in model call ~600 tokens; max we see occasionally ~2k tokens.
- Steady-state QPS: ~60 QPS (weekday afternoons).
- Peak bursts: we've seen up to ~650 QPS for 30–90s during marketing events; rare events have driven ~900 QPS for under a minute.
- Streaming: we need real-time partial token streaming for web UI (low-latency first chunk important). Chunk size doesn't need to be 1 token; 25–75 token chunks are fine.
- SLA: our internal goal is P95 <= 500ms for initial chunk delivery and P99 degradation tolerated during multi-minute outages only.

One other constraint: all customer data must remain in the US region for now.

I'll introduce our infra lead to the PoC thread if Marcus needs deeper telemetry.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Kapoor
Sr. Product Manager, ParcelCo Logistics
samir@parcelco.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir@parcelco.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T01:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: workload breakdown & capacity follow-up

Samir — appreciate the upload and the clarifications. I took a quick pass over the sample trace and sketched a sizing heatmap. Key items below; I'll turn this into the PoC doc (attached) with exact GPU math and an autoscale proposal.

Quick throughput math (ballpark):
- Median request tokens generated: 150–200 tokens. We'll use 200 tokens for conservative sizing.
- Steady-state tokens/sec = 60 QPS * 200 tokens = 12,000 tokens/sec.
- Burst tokens/sec = 650 QPS * 200 tokens = 130,000 tokens/sec (we'll round to 120–140k for safety).

Model & runtime guidance:
- For streaming with P95 <= 500ms we recommend a quantized 8B variant (model label: rdx-8b-q8) with low-latency kernel path. Measured sustainable token throughput for that variant on our optimized runtime is ~40k tokens/sec per GPU under mixed workloads (with KV cache hits and small decoding beams).

Initial GPU count estimates (conservative):
- Steady-state: 12k / 40k ≈ 0.3 GPUs → 1 GPU (to allow headroom, concurrency, and background tasks).
- Peak burst sizing: 130k / 40k ≈ 3.25 GPUs → 4 GPUs to maintain latency headroom and avoid queueing.
- Recommendation: 1 prewarmed primary instance for steady traffic + a warm burst pool with 3 additional prewarmed GPUs that can be brought online (fast scale) for short spikes. If you prefer fewer big nodes vs more small nodes we can adjust; the PoC will include 2x sizing variants (scale-wide and scale-narrow).

Autoscale triggers & warm pools:
- Trigger scaling at sustained 75% GPU utilization over 15s for burst pool expansion.
- Keep 1–2 GPUs in warm standby (preloaded KV caches) to reduce cold start tail latencies for streaming.

Other optimizations to lower unit cost / improve latency:
- Prefix KV caching for repeated context (saves both tokens and latency).
- 50–75 token streaming chunking (Samir said this is acceptable).
- Workload-aware batching for background jobs; real-time streaming paths should avoid large batch waits.

Questions for you before finalizing PoC plan:
1) Confirm the percent of calls that include long generations (500+ tokens). You said ~5–7% — please confirm.
2) Any hard requirement on cold-start recovery time for the burst (e.g., must be <10s)?
3) Who on infra should we include for a quick architecture sync?

Attached: poc-capacity-plan.pdf (draft) — will finalize with exact math and cost estimates once you confirm the few items above.

I'll plan to present the PoC options in our kickoff — propose Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwoodinference.com
